text: Transcript mails come from meetings organised by other people, not only by the mailbox owner. So the Meet Recordings Drive folder of the mailbox owner does not contain them all, and polling Drive for new files is not a viable design. The mailbox is the only place every transcript reliably appears. Told by the user, 2026-09-08.

The Google Meet notification mails in the Transcripts label do NOT contain the summary and action items in the body. Verified against the real mailbox on 2026-09-08: messages are multipart/alternative with text/plain of 4.4-6.0 KB and a text/html part, no file attachments, and a docs.google.com/document/d/ link. The user confirmed the summary and actions live only in the linked Google Doc. This is why the design needs Drive or Docs API access and OAuth, rather than IMAP alone.

Google Docs API access from this Workspace account works. Verified 2026-09-08 with an OAuth desktop-app client and the documents.readonly scope. Two setup traps hit on the way: a Web application OAuth client gives redirect_uri_mismatch because only a Desktop app client accepts http://localhost on an arbitrary port; and an OAuth consent screen left as External/Testing issues refresh tokens that expire after seven days, which would break an hourly cron weekly, so the consent screen must be Internal under the work Workspace.

The linked Gemini notes document is short, about 35 paragraphs, so it is the notes document and not the raw transcript. It does not use HEADING_1 for section labels. Observed on a real document 2026-09-08: four SUBTITLE paragraphs forming a header block (22-39 characters each, so not section labels), 30 NORMAL_TEXT paragraphs, and a single HEADING_2 reading 'Next steps'. There is no 'Summary' or 'Action items' heading, so an extractor keyed on those literal strings would find nothing.

The Gemini notes documents are TABBED Google Docs. Docs API documents.get returns only the first tab in document.body unless includeTabsContent=True is passed, in which case content moves to document.tabs[].documentTab.body.content with nested childTabs. Discovered 2026-09-08 after a Summary heading that was plainly visible in the browser never appeared in API output. Any code reading these documents must request tabs content and walk the tab tree; reading document.body alone silently returns a fragment, which is the dangerous failure mode because it looks like success.

Correction to the 2026-09-08 document and OAuth observations: the initial no-Summary conclusion came from a partial first-tab view and is superseded by the later tab-aware observation. The documents.readonly scope covers every Google Doc accessible to the authorized account, not only documents linked from Gmail. An External consent screen in Production can be used for unattended refresh tokens; Internal consent is not mandatory. The previously recorded OAuth client type and consent settings were not independently verified and must not be treated as proven.
